text: Good morning everyone, please open your notebooks.
Today we are going to learn how green plants prepare their own food.
Animals have to eat other living things, but plants only need sunlight, water and air.
This process of making food with the help of light is what we call photosynthesis.
Plants combine carbon dioxide and water and make a sugar named glucose, and they give out oxygen.
Living things that make their own food are autotrophs, and those that depend on others are heterotrophs.
Now look at the leaf. It is wide and flat so that it can catch a lot of sunlight.
Under the microscope you can see small holes on the lower side of the leaf. These are the stomata.
Guard cells open and close these holes to let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
The green colour of the leaf comes from a pigment called chlorophyll, inside the chloroplasts.
Chlorophyll traps the energy from the sun. Without it the plant cannot make food.
Next, how does water reach the leaf? The roots and root hairs soak it up from the soil.
Water goes up the stem through narrow tubes called xylem.
Some water escapes from the leaves as vapour. This is transpiration, and it keeps the plant cool.
Extra glucose gets changed into starch and stored in roots, seeds and fruits like potatoes and rice.
We can check for starch with iodine. If it turns blue black, starch is present.
Finally, remember that every food chain starts with photosynthesis, and it keeps oxygen in the air.
